messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool "XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement" with arguments:

{
    element: ??? (qualified name)
    augs: augmentations
}

But we have to provide the qualified name as a QName object constructed from namespaceURI, localPart, prefix.

The user says: "with the qualified name {namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}". So we should pass something like new QName("http://www.example.com", "item", "ex") but since it's just a string representation maybe they want us to supply it as such. But the instructions say: "This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation." That means we could give a string representing the QName object. For example: "QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')".

Also "augmentation information `augmentations`" presumably refers to some variable named augmentations; we might refer to it directly.

Thus we will produce JSON payload:

{
   "element": "new javax.xml.namespace.QName(\"http://www.example.com\", \"item\", \"ex\")",
   "augs": "augmentations"
}

Alternatively, we may use the actual class names: "javax.xml.namespace.QName". Provide fully-qualified class name.

Let's check guidelines: In previous examples, they'd used e.g.:

{
  "element":"org.w3c.dom.Element",
  ...
}

So likely we should specify the full class path: "javax.xml.namespace.QName". And then include its constructor args inside parentheses.

Hence:

{
  "element":"javax.xml.namespace.QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')",
  "augs":"augmentations"
}

Yes.

Now let's output accordingly.
